I write Python and call Anthropic directly, with no agent framework. How should I structure tracing for my own tool-calling loop?

smart_toy

Wrap each user request in a turn, each Anthropic messages.create call in an LLM span, and each tool execution in a tool span. Put all of these inside one conversation. This is Weave's agent tracing model, which the docs describe for agents you instrument yourself.

Structure

Conversation and turn: A conversation groups turns by a shared conversation_id. It is not a parent span. Each turn (invoke_agent) is the root span of its own trace and covers one user message and the agent's full reply [S5].
LLM calls and tool calls: A turn can contain many LLM calls (chat), and each LLM call can trigger many tool calls (execute_tool) [S5]. For a loop that runs until the model stops requesting tools, open one LLM span per messages.create call. Open one tool span per requested tool inside the turn. The docs' example shows only two LLM calls per turn (tool decision, then final answer) [S4]. Looping is my extension of that pattern.
Autopatching: The tutorial for hand-instrumenting a bare provider SDK sets settings={"implicitly_patch_integrations": False}. Otherwise the same activity is traced twice, once as your Conversation span and once as a traced Op [S1].

Sketch

This is an untested outline, not a documented Anthropic recipe. TOOLS and run_tool are placeholders for your own tool schemas and dispatcher. The weave calls follow the documented pattern [S1][S4]. The Anthropic message handling is my own sketch.

import weave
from anthropic import Anthropic

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]",
           settings={"implicitly_patch_integrations": False})
client = Anthropic()
MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5"  # use your model

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model=MODEL):
        while True:
            with weave.start_llm(model=MODEL, provider_name="anthropic") as llm:
                resp = client.messages.create(
                    model=MODEL, max_tokens=1024, messages=history, tools=TOOLS)
                llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(
                    input_tokens=resp.usage.input_tokens,
                    output_tokens=resp.usage.output_tokens))
            # Keep the assistant message (including tool_use blocks).
            history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": resp.content})
            tool_uses = [b for b in resp.content if b.type == "tool_use"]
            if not tool_uses:
                return resp
            results = []
            for tu in tool_uses:
                with weave.start_tool(name=tu.name, arguments=str(tu.input),
                                      tool_call_id=tu.id) as tool:
                    tool.result = run_tool(tu.name, tu.input)
                results.append({"type": "tool_result",
                                "tool_use_id": tu.id, "content": tool.result})
            history.append({"role": "user", "content": results})

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent") as conversation:
    history = []
    run_turn(history, "…first question…")

Notes

Tracing does not replace your message history. Keep sending history to the model and append each assistant response. The docs' loop does the same [S4].
Spans are context managers, so nesting follows your with blocks. The docs also describe a try-finally pattern and a manual start/end pattern. I didn't read those sections.
I didn't verify the exact signature of llm.record for Anthropic responses. The docs' examples pass usage, response_id and response_model [S4].

face

For that same setup, how do I record input, output and cache token usage so the trace can show costs?

smart_toy

Pass a weave.Usage to llm.record(...) inside each start_llm span. Set input_tokens to the total input, including cached tokens. Report the cache counts in separate fields, and pass response_model. My earlier sketch left out the cache fields and response_model, so it would likely have shown near-zero cost for cached prompts.

What Weave needs

Complete usage: input_tokens is the total input, including cached tokens. Weave prices cache reads and cache writes at their own rates and subtracts them from that total. So cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens must be reported in addition to a total input_tokens that includes them [S6].
Anthropic reports cached tokens separately from input_tokens: You have to add them back into the total yourself. If you omit them, usage and cost can render as roughly zero [S6].
A priceable model id: Weave prefers response_model and falls back to the model you passed to start_llm. An alias such as sonnet isn't priceable and shows Cost -. Pass the concrete id from resp.model as response_model [S6].

Replace the LLM span in your loop with this

This is adapted from the docs' Anthropic example [S6]. The docs' example makes one call without tools. Here it sits inside your loop, so I dropped llm.output(...) because a tool-calling response may contain tool_use blocks instead of text.

with weave.start_llm(model=MODEL, provider_name="anthropic") as llm:
    resp = client.messages.create(
        model=MODEL, max_tokens=1024, messages=history, tools=TOOLS)
    u = resp.usage
    llm.record(
        usage=weave.Usage(
            input_tokens=u.input_tokens
            + u.cache_read_input_tokens
            + u.cache_creation_input_tokens,
            output_tokens=u.output_tokens,
            cache_read_input_tokens=u.cache_read_input_tokens,
            cache_creation_input_tokens=u.cache_creation_input_tokens,
        ),
        response_id=resp.id,
        response_model=resp.model,
    )

Notes

record(...) applies only the fields you pass. You can also assign properties such as llm.usage individually [S6][S7].
Do this on every LLM span in the loop, not just the last one. Each messages.create call has its own usage.
Pass provider_name="anthropic" explicitly. Weave doesn't infer it from the model string [S7].
Not covered by the docs I read: the Anthropic SDK may return None for the cache fields when caching isn't used. If yours does, use (u.cache_read_input_tokens or 0). This is my own defensive suggestion.
I haven't run this example.
